newsitem.title: USA: Grand Union bonds climb on talks of cash infusion.
newsitem.headline: Grand Union bonds climb on talks of cash infusion.

text.p: Grand Union bonds gained two points on Tuesday after news that negotiations were underway for a $75 million cash infusion at traders said.

"There are negotiations going on for financing," said Michael Sitrick, a spokesman for Shamrock Capital Advisors. He said proceeds would be used to cover the struggling supermarket chain's September interest payment, but declined to comment on the amount of the loan.
Sources close to the deal said the loan would total $75 million.

Trefoil Capital Investors II LP, a Shamrock-managed investment vehicle for Roy E. Disney's family, and General Electric's GE Private Placement Partners II, agreed last year to purchase $100 million in Grand Union preferred stock.

"I think the characterization of this as an emergency loan is not only a bit hysterical, it's overstated," said a source close to the deal, referring to newspaper accounts of the circumstances surrounding the loan.
The source said Soros Fund Management LLC and Cargill Corp would be part of a non-exclusive consortium of investors. Soros Fund Management LLC and Cargill Corp declined to comment on the report.

In recent weeks, talk of a possible loan boosted Grand Union's bonds which had been trading sharply lower on rumors the company would default on a $39 million interest payment in September. Bonds rallied from the high 30's to the 50's over that time period, market sources said.
Grand Union 12 percent bonds were quoted higher on Tuesday at 51-1/2 bid, 52 offer, traders said.

Just two months ago, Grand Union's 12 percent paper was trading in the high 80's area, but continued deterioration in the firm's operating performance prompted both Standard & Poor's and Moody's Investors Service to downgrade its credit ratings.
In August, Moody's cut Grand Union's bank facility rating to B3 from B2 and its senior unsecured debt to Caa3 from Caa1.
Moody's said the rating action was prompted by Grand Union's announcement that due to the shortfall in its operating performance it was in default of of the financial covenants in its bank agreement.

In addition, Moody's said the ratings downgrade reflected the deterioration in the firm's operating performance over the last several quarters and the expectation that performance will remain well below historic levels going forward.
S&P rates Grand Union's bank facility rating at B-minus and senior unsecured debt at CCC.
A Grand Union spokesman declined to comment on the loan.
Grand Union, which emerged from bankruptcy in June, 1995 after filing Chapter 11 in January 1995, is one of the largest operators of supermarkets in the northeast, with 224 stores in six states.
